subject: Tranche prioritization & baseline for AuroraCloud launch
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@auroracloud.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Carlos Mendes <c.mendes@brightai.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Jan 2028 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Launch capacity asks — Q1 peak forecast attached

Tessa — thanks again for the call earlier. As discussed, AuroraCloud is accelerating our public beta and we now have a hard launch window in mid-February. I attached an updated demand forecast for the first 8 weeks (Aurora_Demand_Forecast_Q1.xlsx).

Short version: peak generation requests are likely to hit 45% of an entire 8xA100 pool for a sustained 72-hour window during the first week, with a steady-state baseline at ~12% thereafter. We understand you have existing Dedicated commitments (including BrightAI) and want to avoid being disruptive — but we need clarity on guaranteed baseline plus burst.

Key asks:
- Confirm whether Redwood can guarantee a reserved baseline for Aurora starting Feb 10 (minimum 20% of an 8x A100 tranche)
- If guaranteed burst is available, what are the limits and expected latency SLOs?
- Lead time and SOW for adding a tranche/priority policy

Appreciate a rapid read. If needed I can join a brief call tomorrow.

— Samantha
Samantha Lee
Head of ML Platform, AuroraCloud
Attachments: Aurora_Demand_Forecast_Q1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 98KB)
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@auroracloud.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Jan 2028 10:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Launch capacity asks — Q1 peak forecast attached

Thanks Samantha — looping in Ben and Karthik to surface constraints and options. High level, two paths: guaranteed reserved baseline (contractually committed GPUs) or a best-effort burst-capacity commitment with credits and higher latency risk.

Ben / Karthik — summary of Aurora ask below (from attachment): baseline ~12% sustained, 72-hr peak at ~45% of an 8xA100 tranche starting Feb 10. They want baseline guarantee for launch plus some burst headroom. Can you sketch the operational limits and an allocation proposal this morning? Include impact to current Dedicated customers (notably BrightAI) and a recommended prioritized policy (percent reserved, burst ceiling, preemption behavior).

We need to respond with a proposal and a timeline for SOW + DocuSign link by EOD. Samantha — if we can provide a 14-day guaranteed baseline + burst policy that scales to peak for a short window, is that workable from your side?

Thanks,
Tessa
Director, Account Strategy — Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Jan 2028 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Internal: quick allocation sketch for Aurora

Tessa / Karthik — ran numbers against current tranche inventory. Short take: we have three 8xA100 tranches in the west-us pool allocated as follows today:
- Tranche A: BrightAI (monthly committed) — baseline reservation 40%
- Tranche B: Reserved pool (multi-tenant burst) — flexible 60%
- Tranche C: Overflow + canary workloads — 0% reserved

If we carve Aurora a guaranteed baseline of 20% on a new micro-tranche (effectively creating Tranche D) that reduces headroom in the flexible pool and increases contention risk for BrightAI during their scheduled jobs. I attached an Allocation_Impact_Matrix.csv that models latency degradation and token-cost impact across scenarios.

Proposal (fast):
1) Offer Aurora a 20% guaranteed baseline on a 8xA100 micro-tranche for 14 days starting Feb 10.
2) Allow a burst policy up to additional 25% of the tranche for a 72-hr window with weighted preemption (BrightAI jobs are lower-priority during the burst window but get full runback credits).
3) In exchange: require a short SOW addendum committing to launch week compensation + a 60-day notice to scale down.

Consequence: BrightAI will see ~10–15% latency deterioration for queued massive batches if they align with Aurora's 72-hr peak; ops can mitigate with temporary job re-routing but that adds scheduling complexity.

If leadership signs off, I can draft the amendment and mark affected customers for a heads-up.

—Ben
Senior Sales Operations — Redwood Inference
Attachments: Allocation_Impact_Matrix.csv (spreadsheet, 24KB)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Jan 2028 13:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Internal: quick allocation sketch for Aurora

Adding technical constraints:
- West-US pool currently has 24 physical A100 GPUs (3 x 8x tranches). Our scheduler supports soft priorities but reserved baselines require pre-warm KV caches; spinning up a new micro-tranche will take ~6 hours to reach steady-state inference throughput for large models.
- Burst windows are possible, but sustained 72-hr bursts at +25% will increase node temperatures and reduce headroom for autoscaling; ops prefers to limit sustained burst to 48 hours unless we allocate additional physical capacity.

Operational suggestion:
- Offer Aurora 20% reserved baseline + a hardened burst option (up to 25%) capped at 48 hours. For any extension to 72 hours, require explicit ops sign-off and a nominal premium.
- Implement weighted-priority policy that preempts non-latency-sensitive batch jobs (match by job tag). We will add a canary routing rule so BrightAI can opt-in to run sensitive batches outside Aurora's peak windows for a 10% credits return.

If Tessa approves, I'll feed this to the SRE runbook and prep the SOW language clarifying warm-up time, burst caps, thermal caveats, and service credits.

—Karthik
Head of Infrastructure Planning — Redwood Inference
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@auroracloud.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Jan 2028 16:32:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Launch capacity asks — Q1 peak forecast attached

Samantha — thanks for the patience. Internal alignment complete; below is our offer and next steps. Quoting prior notes for context.

Offer summary (what Redwood will commit):
- Baseline: 20% reserved on a new 8xA100 micro-tranche, guaranteed from Feb 10 for 14 days. Warm-up time ~6 hours; please schedule your heavy ramp accordingly.
- Burst: up to +25% of the tranche for peak windows, capped at 48 hours without extra premium. For extensions to 72 hours, we require a premium and ops sign-off (we can negotiate).
- Preemption/priority: weighted-priority policy — latency-sensitive BrightAI workloads will be deprioritized during Aurora burst windows but receive runback credits (up to 10% of their monthly invoice) for impacted batches.
- Contract: SOW addendum + DocuSign link (https://docusign.com/tx/7a8b9c-sow-aurora). We will include the warm-up clause and burst cap in the SOW.

Next steps for Aurora:
1) Confirm acceptance of the baseline + burst terms by Tue, Jan 17 COB.
2) Sign SOW via DocuSign.
3) Provide final ramp schedule so ops can pre-warm caches 6 hours ahead.

Ben / Karthik — please prepare the SOW draft (SOW_Aurora_v2.pdf), update the Allocation_Impact_Matrix and flag BrightAI customer success for a heads-up email. Samantha — attaching the forecast and matrix for transparency.

Appreciate it — we want this to be low-friction for Aurora while preserving fairness across committed customers.

—Tessa
Director, Account Strategy — Redwood Inference
Attachments: SOW_Aurora_v2.pdf, Aurora_Demand_Forecast_Q1.xlsx, Allocation_Impact_Matrix.csv
